THE HOLLOW STITCH NURSERY
 DEPARTMENT OF UNNATURAL FAUNA
RECOVERED ARCHIVE
There are creatures in this world that existed long before the Hollow Stitch Nursery. The Nursery
did not create the things in these records - at least, not most of them. Before its halls became
associated with stitched toys, abandoned experiments, and things that learned to breathe without
lungs, it maintained another purpose: collection. Reports arrived from forests, mountains, swamps,
rivers, deserts, and forgotten roads. Investigators were dispatched. Witnesses were interviewed.
Tracks were measured. Samples were collected. When possible, specimens were brought home.
HOW TO READ THE FILES
Each cryptid entry preserves the traditional legend first, followed by the surviving Hollow Stitch
record. Nursery classifications describe only what its investigators claimed to observe. OBSERVED
means staff reported direct contact. TRACKED means an active investigation was maintained.
RECOVERED means physical evidence was obtained. CONFIRMED means the archive contains
evidence the Nursery considered sufficient. CONTAINED is the classification no archivist wanted
to see beside the word escaped.
ARCHIVIST NOTICE
Traditional accounts have been preserved as inspiration whenever possible, but legends vary across
communities and generations. The Hollow Stitch material is fictional and should not be mistaken
for a claim about the cultures or traditions behind these creatures. One instruction appears
repeatedly throughout the recovered field manuals: Do not assume folklore is inaccurate simply
because it is impossible. When generations of people agree that a place, sound, road, or stretch of
water should be left alone, the Nursery's safest recommendation was usually the simplest one: leave
it alone.
Thirty files were recovered. The original inventory lists more.
HOLLOW STITCH NURSERY - ARCHIVE COPY 5

EL SILBÓN
The Whistling One
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-001
 CLASSIFICATION
Cursed Revenant / Death Herald
 THREAT LEVEL
V - EXTREME
 ORIGIN
The Llanos of Venezuela and Colombia
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Acoustic disorientation; relentless pursuit
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Dogs and protective customs in traditional accounts
 STATUS
CONFIRMED - Never contained
LEGEND
Across the plains of Venezuela and Colombia, travelers tell of El Silbon, an impossibly thin wanderer
carrying a sack of bones. His whistle is the warning and the trap. When it sounds close, he may still be far
away. When it sounds faint, tradition warns that he may already be near. Stories describe a cursed spirit
doomed to roam the night, his bones knocking together as he walks.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
The Nursery's first file began with an unmarked package containing seven photographs. Six showed empty
roads. The seventh showed a thin figure with a sack. Three nights later, staff heard a whistle beyond the
western fence. At sunrise, a human finger bone rested against the door. Seven bones appeared over the
following weeks. Years later, investigator Thomas Reed vanished while tracking the Whistler. An eighth
bone arrived six months afterward with Reed's identification tag tied around it. Someone had scratched one
number beneath his name: 8.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
Do not investigate the whistle. Do not whistle back. Count everyone inside. If the second count does not
match the first, do not count again.

EMELA-NTOUKA
 The Killer of Elephants
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-002
 CLASSIFICATION
Swamp Megafauna / Folkloric Beast
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Central African folklore, especially Congo Basin accounts
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Massive strength; aggressive horn-first charge
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Deep water and dense terrain may limit a charge
 STATUS
TRACKED - No living specimen
LEGEND
Emela-Ntouka is traditionally described as a heavy, semi-aquatic beast of the Congo Basin, often compared
to a rhinoceros-like animal with a single horn. Its name is commonly rendered as the 'killer of elephants,'
reflecting stories of a territorial creature powerful enough to attack much larger animals. Reports place it
near remote rivers, marshes, and flooded forest where visibility is poor and escape routes are worse.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Nursery Field Team 2 followed a trail of broken reeds to a mud bank scored by a single deep groove. The
prints beside it did not match any known animal in the expedition guide. At dusk, something struck their
supply canoe from beneath the water and drove it onto shore. A horn fragment was later recovered from
the hull. Laboratory notes end after one sentence: 'Sample continues to grow after removal.' The fragment
was transferred to Cold Cabinet C. Cabinet C is now listed as empty.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If the reeds bend toward you instead of away, leave the water immediately.

THE AHOOL
The Cry Above the Canopy
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-003
 CLASSIFICATION
Aerial Cryptid / Giant Chiropteran
 THREAT LEVEL
III - HIGH
 ORIGIN
Java, Indonesia
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Silent approach followed by powerful aerial attack
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Bright light and enclosed spaces
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Capture failed
LEGEND
The Ahool is a legendary winged creature reported from Java. Accounts often describe an enormous
bat-like animal with a broad wingspan and a distinctive cry said to sound like 'ahool.' Sightings are
associated with dense rainforest, waterfalls, and river valleys where a large creature could pass overhead and
vanish into the canopy before witnesses could make sense of what they saw.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
The Nursery installed sound recorders along a river gorge after three nights of identical cries. On the fourth
night, every recorder activated at once. The microphones captured one call, then forty-two seconds of
wingbeats without a visible source. A field technician disappeared before sunrise. His lantern was found
hanging thirty feet above the ground in a tree with no climb marks on the trunk. The final recorder
contained a second voice beneath the Ahool's cry - the missing technician whispering, 'Don't look up.'
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If the call repeats from directly overhead, extinguish your light and move under cover.

THE BATSQUATCH
 The Winged Ape of the Cascades
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-004
 CLASSIFICATION
Aerial Hominid / Mountain Cryptid
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Pacific Northwest, United States
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Flight; exceptional strength; rapid vertical movement
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Unknown
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Active reports
LEGEND
Batsquatch stories describe a large, ape-like creature with leathery wings, glowing or unusual eyes, and a
powerful build. Reports are most closely associated with the forests and mountains of the Pacific Northwest,
where witnesses have described a shape too large for a bat and too airborne for anything resembling a
primate.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Hollow Stitch observers placed bait near a high ridge after repeated night sightings. Nothing touched it for
six days. On the seventh morning the bait cage was found crushed flat from above, though there were no
tracks around it. A strip of dark membrane clung to the steel. During transport, the sample began twitching
whenever the vehicle passed beneath power lines. It vanished from the evidence locker that night. The
ceiling vent above the locker was still screwed shut from the inside.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
Do not assume the tree line is the boundary of the search. Check above it.

THE BUNYIP
The Thing Beneath Still Water
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-005
 CLASSIFICATION
Aquatic Folkloric Entity
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Aboriginal Australian traditions
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Possible alteration of witness perception and memory
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Avoids prolonged disturbance of its water
 STATUS
TRACKED - Recovery failed
LEGEND
Bunyip traditions are associated with swamps, billabongs, creeks, and waterholes in Australia. Descriptions
vary dramatically - fur, scales, tusks, flippers, long necks, and stranger forms all appear in different
accounts. The Hollow Stitch archive notes that conflicting descriptions may be part of the phenomenon
rather than evidence against it.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Three Nursery investigators entered a wetland carrying cameras, sonar gear, and reinforced restraints.
Their final radio transmission records all three arguing about the creature's appearance. One described fur,
one scales, and one insisted it had no head. Then a fourth voice asked, 'Which one of you is standing in the
water?' Only three investigators were assigned. None returned. Divers later recovered a Nursery
identification badge belonging to no known employee. Written across the back: WE SHOULD HAVE LEFT
IT THERE.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If every witness describes a different animal, stop deciding who is wrong. Leave the water.

CADBOROSAURUS
 Caddy of the Pacific Coast
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-006
 CLASSIFICATION
Marine Serpent / Coastal Cryptid
 THREAT LEVEL
III - HIGH
 ORIGIN
Pacific coast of North America
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
High-speed swimming; prolonged submersion
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Unknown
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Uncontained
LEGEND
Cadborosaurus, often called 'Caddy,' is a sea-serpent legend associated with the Pacific coast of North
America. Witnesses have described a long-bodied marine animal with a horse-like or camel-like head,
visible humps, and a serpentine neck. Reports cluster around channels, islands, and coastal waters where a
large animal can disappear quickly beneath deep water.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
A Nursery research vessel tracked a repeating sonar contact for ninety minutes. The contact circled the boat
without surfacing, then matched the vessel's speed exactly. When the engines stopped, it stopped. When
they reversed, it reversed. The final sonar print showed the contact directly beneath the hull and a second,
much larger shape below it. The captain ended the operation immediately. Someone later wrote in the
margin: 'We were not tracking the adult.'
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If the sonar contact begins matching your movements, end the survey.

CRESSIE
The Serpent of Crescent Lake
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-007
 CLASSIFICATION
Freshwater Serpent / Lake Cryptid
 THREAT LEVEL
II - MODERATE
 ORIGIN
Newfoundland, Canada
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Long-duration submersion; sudden surface movement
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Unknown
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Nonaggressive
LEGEND
Cressie is the name given to a long-bodied lake creature reported from Crescent Lake in Newfoundland.
Descriptions vary, but many accounts involve a serpentine animal moving just below the surface or leaving
an unusual wake. Unlike more openly violent water legends, Cressie is usually described as elusive rather
than predatory.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Nursery observers recorded an elongated wake crossing a calm inlet without any visible animal at its head. A
floating camera was deployed the next morning. It returned to shore on its own three hours later, lens
cracked and memory card missing. The camera body contained lake water on the outside and dry sand
inside the sealed battery compartment. No one could explain the sand. Crescent Lake has no shoreline
matching the mineral sample.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
Observation only. Do not pursue submerged movement into narrow water.
�����������������������������������������������������
END FILE HSN-CR-007

THE DOVER DEMON
 The Roadside Watcher
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-008
 CLASSIFICATION
Unclassified Humanoid / Nocturnal Entity
 THREAT LEVEL
III - HIGH
 ORIGIN
Dover, Massachusetts, United States
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Extreme agility; low-light movement
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Avoids prolonged exposure and groups
 STATUS
CONFIRMED SIGHTING - No capture
LEGEND
The Dover Demon legend began with a cluster of reported encounters near Dover, Massachusetts, in 1977.
Witnesses described a small, thin humanoid with a large smooth head, long fingers, and glowing or
reflective eyes. It was seen near roads, walls, and wooded areas, appearing only briefly before disappearing
into the dark.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
A Hollow Stitch investigator reconstructed the original route and placed trail cameras along a stone wall. At
2:17 A.M., every camera captured the same figure at the same instant, despite being spaced nearly half a mile
apart. In each image the creature faced the camera. In the final frame it was gone, replaced by a close
photograph of the investigator asleep in his motel room. The motel door had remained locked all night.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If it stops moving when observed, do not approach. It may be waiting for you to look away.

THE FLATWOODS MONSTER
 The Spade-Headed Visitor
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-009
 CLASSIFICATION
Extraterrestrial / Atmospheric Entity
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Flatwoods, West Virginia, United States
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Gliding movement; chemical or noxious emission
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Unknown
 STATUS
RECORDED - Origin unresolved
LEGEND
The Flatwoods Monster entered American folklore after a 1952 encounter in West Virginia. Witnesses
described a tall figure with a dark body, glowing eyes, and a head or hood shaped like a spade or ace. The
encounter was also associated with a strange odor that reportedly caused nausea and irritation.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Nursery chemists obtained a soil sample from the reported encounter area. When warmed, the sample
released a sharp metallic odor and caused every compass in the laboratory to point toward the Nursery
basement instead of north. The effect lasted eleven minutes. During those eleven minutes, a sealed
basement door opened by itself. Security found no intruder - only a triangular burn mark on the floor and a
smell matching the sample.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If the air smells metallic and your compass turns toward the building, evacuate the lower level.

THE FOUKE MONSTER
 The Boggy Creek Beast
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-010
 CLASSIFICATION
Hominid Cryptid / Swamp Stalker
 THREAT LEVEL
III - HIGH
 ORIGIN
Arkansas, United States
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Exceptional strength; silent movement through swamp terrain
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Avoids sustained pursuit
 STATUS
TRACKED - Evidence recovered
LEGEND
The Fouke Monster, also known as the Boggy Creek Monster, is associated with reports near Fouke,
Arkansas. Witnesses have described a large, hairy, ape-like creature moving through swamp and woodland.
Tracks, strange calls, and close encounters helped make the creature one of the best-known regional
cryptids in the United States.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Nursery trackers followed a line of three-toed impressions through knee-deep mud. The tracks ended at a
cypress tree with no prints leaving the area. Thirty feet above them, the bark had been stripped away in long
parallel gouges. A hair sample recovered from the trunk contained keratin but no usable cellular material.
Under magnification, every strand appeared hollow. One strand produced a low knocking sound when
sealed inside a glass vial.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If the tracks stop without turning, check the trees before checking behind you.
�����������������������������������������������������
END FILE HSN-CR-010

THE GBAHALI
 The River Armor
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-011
 CLASSIFICATION
Reptilian Cryptid / River Predator
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
West African regional accounts
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Armored body; powerful bite and tail
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Unknown
 STATUS
RECOVERED EVIDENCE - Specimen unconfirmed
LEGEND
The Gbahali is described in regional West African cryptid accounts as a large reptilian creature, sometimes
compared to a crocodile-like animal with unusual armor or prehistoric features. Stories place it near rivers
and forest waterways, where its heavy body and powerful tail would make it dangerous at close range.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
A Nursery expedition recovered a single plate of blackened keratin from a riverbank. The plate was too
thick to cut with field tools. Back at Hollow Stitch, technicians discovered that it grew warmer whenever
water was poured nearby. During a storm, the evidence room flooded by less than an inch. The plate
disappeared. A wet drag mark crossed the floor and ended at a wall with no door, pipe, or opening.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
Do not store recovered armor below ground level or within hearing distance of running water.
�����������������������������������������������������
END FILE HSN-CR-011
NIGHTMARE CRYPTIDS - HOLLOW STITCH ARCHIVE 26

[PDF TEXT PAGE 28]
THE GOWROW
 The Ozark Cave Terror
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-012
 CLASSIFICATION
Cave Reptile / Regional Cryptid
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Ozark folklore, United States
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Ambush from caves; heavy crushing strength
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Limited maneuverability in open ground
 STATUS
TRACKED - Lair not secured
LEGEND
The Gowrow is an Ozark monster legend described as a large reptilian or dragon-like creature associated
with caves, hollows, and remote country. Accounts vary widely, but many emphasize a long body,
dangerous teeth, and a habit of emerging from hidden places where people would rather not follow.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Nursery surveyors mapped a cave after livestock vanished near its entrance. Their chalk marks began
reappearing ahead of them, as if another team were copying the route from deeper inside. At the final
chamber they found a pile of bones and one fresh Nursery chalk stick broken in half. No member of the
team had lost one. They withdrew. When they returned the next day, the cave entrance had collapsed -
outward.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
If your route markers appear ahead of you, the survey is over.
�����������������������������������������������������
END FILE HSN-CR-012
NIGHTMARE CRYPTIDS - HOLLOW STITCH ARCHIVE 28

[PDF TEXT PAGE 30]
THE INKANYAMBA
 The Storm Serpent
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-013
 CLASSIFICATION
Aquatic Serpent / Weather Entity
 THREAT LEVEL
V - EXTREME
 ORIGIN
Zulu and Xhosa traditions, Southern Africa
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Storm association; violent aquatic movement
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Unknown
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Containment prohibited
LEGEND
Inkanyamba traditions describe a vast serpent-like being associated with deep water and severe storms in
Southern Africa. It is often linked to waterfalls, lakes, and violent weather, with accounts suggesting that its
movement and anger may be reflected in the sky itself.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
A Nursery observation team arrived during clear weather and deployed cameras near a waterfall pool.
Twelve minutes later, barometric pressure dropped sharply and cloud cover formed directly above the site.
One camera caught a long dark shape rising through the mist. The next frame was completely white. The
storm destroyed every instrument except a mechanical pressure gauge, which remained fixed at a reading
below the minimum printed on its dial.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
No capture operations. If the pressure falls without a forecasted storm, evacuate the basin.
�����������������������������������������������������
END FILE HSN-CR-013
NIGHTMARE CRYPTIDS - HOLLOW STITCH ARCHIVE 30

[PDF TEXT PAGE 32]
THE KONGAMATO
 The Breaker of Boats
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-014
 CLASSIFICATION
Aerial Reptilian Cryptid
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Central and Southern African regional stories
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
High-speed aerial strike over waterways
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Dense vegetation may restrict takeoff and landing
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Active reports
LEGEND
Kongamato stories describe a dangerous flying reptile seen near rivers and swamps in parts of Central and
Southern Africa. Witnesses often describe leathery wings, a long jaw, and sudden attacks on boats or people
near the water. The creature is frequently compared to a pterosaur-like animal, though no physical
specimen has been verified.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
A Nursery canoe team heard wingbeats moments before something struck the rear of their boat hard
enough to split the wood. The attack repeated three times from different directions. No creature was visible
until a camera accidentally fired while pointed straight upward. The photograph showed a winged shape
descending - and a second shadow above it, much larger than the first.
NURSERY DIRECTIVE
When the first wingbeat is heard, leave open water. The second may already be descending.
�����������������������������������������������������
END FILE HSN-CR-014
NIGHTMARE CRYPTIDS - HOLLOW STITCH ARCHIVE 32

[PDF TEXT PAGE 34]
THE KUSHTAKA
 The Otter Man
H.S.N. FILE
HSN-CR-015
 CLASSIFICATION
Shapeshifting Spirit / Coastal Entity
 THREAT LEVEL
IV - SEVERE
 ORIGIN
Tlingit traditions, Alaska and Pacific Northwest
 DOCUMENTED ABILITY
Shapeshifting; mimicry; lure behavior
 OBSERVED WEAKNESS
Traditional protections vary by account
 STATUS
OBSERVED - Interaction restricted
LEGEND
Kushtaka traditions come from the Tlingit people of the Pacific Northwest and Alaska. The beings are often
described as otter-like shapeshifters able to mimic human voices, lure travelers, and move between human
and animal forms. Accounts vary from dangerous tricksters to beings that can rescue or transform the lost.
HOLLOW STITCH RECORD
Nursery staff investigating a coastal disappearance heard a child calling from across an inlet after midnight.
